title: Pre-Analysis — Electronic Control Unit Mounting Standard Offered to the Auran 7000 Fleet
abstract: Closed work order on offering the wire rope isolator mounting and ventilated shroud standard to the Auran 7000 powered aircraft. Rejected outright: the nacelle interface, the cooling path and the cowl volume are all different.

sections.objective: Determine whether the isolator mounting and ventilated thermal shroud standard developed for the Auran 7700 installation can be offered to the Auran 7000 powered SOLANO-38 and SOLANO-39 aircraft, following two control unit power supply failures reported on the newer fleet with a similar signature. The work order had to compare the mounting interface, the shroud cooling path and the soak temperature evidence before any effectivity extension was considered.
sections.findings_summary: The comparison did not hold anywhere it mattered. The shroud draws its cooling air from a fan cowl position that the noise attenuation blanket proposal for the newer engine fills with acoustic material, and the two occupy the same cowl zone; on the newer installation the shroud would sit in still air. The retrofit bulletin is written entirely around the older nacelle interface and its torque values, and nothing in it transfers. The removal and installation tasks are equally specific, down to the isolator preload sequence; a Auran 7000 version would be a new task, not an effectivity line. The one genuinely useful result came from similarity rather than entities: the aft pylon fairing heat shield work had already characterised the recirculation behaviour that drives the soak temperature, in completely different language, and that evidence should feed a properly scoped modification for the newer engine.
sections.next_steps: Reject the extension and close the question against this modification. Raise a separate proposal for the Auran 7000 installation with its own thermal survey, using the pylon fairing recirculation evidence as the starting point rather than the Auran 7700 soak data. Coordinate the cowl volume with the noise attenuation proposal before any shroud geometry is drawn, and tell the reporting operators that the two power supply failures need their own investigation rather than a retrofit.

similarity_seeds: vibration and soak temperature shortening the life of a control unit power supply
ventilated shroud drawing cooling air through a fan cowl position

tasks.title: Compare the mounting interface between the two engine installations
Trace the shroud cooling path in the newer fan cowl
Search for existing thermal evidence in the nacelle and pylon area
Assess transferability of the retrofit instructions

expected_findings.rationale: The noise attenuation proposal fills the fan cowl position the ventilated shroud draws its cooling air from, in the same cowl zone. On the newer installation the shroud would sit in still air and lose the mechanism it exists for. Nothing in the two texts overlaps; only the zone connects them.
expected_findings.resolution: Coordinate the cowl volume before any shroud geometry is drawn for the newer engine.

expected_findings.rationale: The retrofit vehicle is written around the older nacelle interface, its bracket pattern and its torque values. There is no line in it that an effectivity extension could reuse, so an extension would in practice be a new bulletin.
expected_findings.resolution: Leave the bulletin effectivity as it stands.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task gives the isolator preload sequence against the older mounting frame. A newer engine version is a new task, not an effectivity line, and writing it as a variant would make both harder to follow.
expected_findings.resolution: No change here; scope a separate task under the new proposal.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by similarity alone and by nothing else. One text is about heat shield distortion and hot gas recirculation into a fairing cavity; the other is about vibration and soak temperature on an electronics box. They share no part number, FIN, drawing, zone or chapter, and no reader would connect them by title.

expected_findings.rationale: The pylon fairing work already characterised the recirculation behaviour that sets the soak temperature at this end of the nacelle. That evidence is directly usable for a properly scoped proposal on the newer engine and was not known to the requesting office.
expected_findings.resolution: Use the recirculation evidence as the starting point for the new proposal's thermal survey.

expected_non_findings.reason: Ranks well on any search combining heat damage and the pylon fairing, and shares the ATA 54-50 context with the recirculation evidence. It is a composite scarf repair for skin damage and says nothing about the control unit mounting, the shroud or the soak environment.

type_data.conclusion: Extension rejected. The mounting interface, the cooling path and the retrofit instructions are all specific to the older installation; a separate proposal with its own thermal survey is required.
